extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff and hearing officers
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order implementing an interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 based on a felony conviction, with procedural directions for referral, limited recognition, filing an answer, and administrative actions (PKI/customer number dissociation, publication, notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, the interim suspension of Respondent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office is hereby ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim suspension may be ordered when the OED Director requests suspension predicated on evidence that the respondent committed a serious crime (here, a felony). The Order finds no genuine issue of material fact and implements the suspension effective the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious crime / felony conviction as predicate for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order is predicated on Respondent having pled guilty to one felony count of Leaving the Scene of an Accident Involving Personal Injury or Death (Va. Code Ann. § 46.2-894), and the OED Director requested suspension on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A conviction (or plea) for a felony or other 'serious crime' can support a request for interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25; the Order explicitly cites the criminal conviction as the basis for disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of Disciplinary Complaint for formal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint (a copy attached) is referred, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5), to a hearing officer at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral initiates formal adjudicative proceedings before an administrative hearing officer; the Complaint is to be answered as directed (see filing requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25
rubrics_metrics.description: Given Respondent's response stipulating he 'is not aware of any information supporting a genuine issue of material fact' with respect to specified paragraphs of the Notice and Order, the Director determines there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent's stipulation or failure to raise material factual disputes can support the Director's determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists, justifying interim suspension without further factual hearing on that predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office commencing on the date of this Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Order is signed, with such limited recognition being granted for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly time-limited and limited in purpose (to allow compliance with suspension-related responsibilities), not a general restoration of privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a written answer within thirty (30) days (37 C.F.R. § 11.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.36, within thirty (30) days from the date of this Final Order, Respondent's written answer to the Complaint shall be filed with the hearing officer at the specified HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals addresses and a PDF version emailed to the hearing office; a copy must be served on the OED Director by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order gives precise filing addresses (mail and hand-delivery) for the HUD Docket Clerk, requires emailing a PDF to the hearing office, and requires serving a copy on the OED Director (Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO). Compliance with these procedural filing and service instructions is mandatory and jurisdictional for the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette: Notice of Interim Suspension describing the respondent (name, registration number), the fact of interim suspension pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59, and the underlying criminal conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice text is to be published and disciplinary decisions are made available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (link provided). Publication serves public notice of the interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to relevant governmental and bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director gives notice of this Final Order to i) appropriate employees of the USPTO; ii) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and iii) appropriate authorities of any state in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires transmitting the disciplinary action to institutional and state authorities likely to be interested or have regulatory responsibilities for the respondent's license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 contains responsibilities of suspended practitioners (e.g., notice to clients, transfer of files); the Order explicitly imposes that regulatory compliance obligation on the respondent during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of respondent from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative actions will be taken to remove practical access and association (customer numbers, PKI) to prevent the suspended individual from using USPTO electronic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being associated with USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a continuing prohibition tied to the suspension period and reinstatement status; it prevents circumvention of suspension by proxy or new applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of suspension does not stay the suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks a review of this suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal or review does not automatically stay the interim suspension; the suspension remains effective pending review unless and until stayed by proper authority.
